purpose: Distinguish small-input amortization from road structure and weight magnitude in the one-node ACIC/Wasp gap.
predictions: If input size alone explains the road gap, mesh24-z (67.1M edges) should have a similar ACIC/Wasp ratio to road-usa-z (57.7M edges) at one node.
If native weight magnitude alone explains the road gap, dividing road weights by four while scaling both engines' bucket widths should greatly improve the ACIC/Wasp ratio.
A road-specific latency/work-availability limit predicts more controller rounds and a larger Wasp gap than on the similarly sized mesh, even if the weight-scaled road retains its gap.
machine: One exclusive Delta cpu-interactive node, ACIC 16 processes x 7 workers, Wasp independently tuned on two training sources.

graphs.name: road-usa-z
graphs.selection: Frozen from the completed Delta road study; no new search.

correctness: Every solve must match its graph's independent full-graph digest. ACIC process count, scheduler and profile must be checked from each log.
scope: A bounded attribution screen, not an optimization acceptance or a global Wasp tuning claim.
